issuer: Saskatchewan Government Insurance (SGI), through motor licence issuers
note: SGI's pages, rendered in a browser because their text loads by script (read 2026-10-30): a Saskatchewan driver's licence lasts five years and costs $100 paid up front (or five annual payments of $25); a new driver takes a Novice 1 licence from 16, holds it 6 months, then a Novice 2 licence for 12 months before graduating to an experienced Class 5 licence, so a full licence is kept from 18 (17½ rounded up). The photo ID page says a non-driver's first card is free, expires after five years and costs $15 to renew; the first card's fee, nothing, is held.

sources.title: SGI, Renew your licence
sources.said: Your Saskatchewan driver’s licence lasts for five years. ... You can pay for the entire five years up-front for a cost of $100.

sources.title: SGI, New Class 5 drivers
sources.said: to apply for a Class 5 Novice 1 driver's licence, you must: be 16 years ... Continue to practice driving as a Novice 1 driver for 6 months under the GDL driving restrictions. ... you can practice driving for 12 months under the GDL driving restrictions. ... You graduate from the GDL program to an experienced Class 5 driver's licence.

sources.title: SGI, Photo ID
sources.said: Your first card is free if you’ve never had a Saskatchewan photo ID card or driver’s licence before. ... Photo ID cards expire after five years. ... It costs $15 to renew the card.
